comparison: Both strongly support the species-specific effects of bacteria on viral transmission (C3-C5, C38-C40, C50-C52). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative evidence and statistical analysis, while peer reviewers affirm the findings are 'convincing' with 'solid support.' High agreement on core transmission data.

Both support the three-order-of-magnitude dose-response differences (C6-C7, C42-C43, C46). OpenEval details the FISH confirmation and replicate experiments, while peer reviewers explicitly validate the 'several orders of magnitude' quantitative finding. Complete agreement on this dramatic effect size.

Perfect claim overlap (C47-C49, C57-C59) on pharyngeal pumping data. Both support the conclusion that feeding behavior differences don't explain viral susceptibility effects. Editor explicitly affirms these control experiments rule out nutrition as a confounding factor.

Perfect claim overlap (C63-C68) on pathogenicity/lifespan data. Both support the dissociation between bacterial pathogenicity and viral susceptibility effects. Editor explicitly validates these control experiments ruling out pathogenicity as the primary mechanism.

Perfect claim overlap (C69-C71) on plasmid-based replication system. Both support the conclusion that bacteria don't affect viral replication directly. Peer reviewers affirm methodological rigor, though Reviewer 3 notes normalization concerns for related qPCR data (C73).

Perfect claim overlap (C72-C74) on qPCR replication data. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, but peer review is UNCERTAIN due to Reviewer 3's methodological concern about lack of reference gene normalization, which could affect quantitative interpretation of viral load.

Both address viral stability data (C75-C77). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while peer review also SUPPORTED. Both accept the stability findings, though OpenEval notes the interpretation about recovery differences could benefit from additional validation.

Both address viral shedding data (C78-C80). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to speculative interpretation of fourfold difference, while peer reviewers SUPPORT the findings without challenge. Modest disagreement on strength of conclusions from shedding data.

Both address quorum sensing genetic analysis (C85-C86, C88). OpenEval emphasizes mutant phenotype data, peer reviewers explicitly affirm quorum sensing role. Also relates to R4 (exopolysaccharide negative results C87, C89). Strong agreement on quorum sensing mechanisms.

Addresses exopolysaccharide negative results (C87, C89, C95). Both support these negative findings. Peer reviewers don't challenge the conclusion that exopolysaccharides are not involved, consistent with OpenEval's SUPPORTED rating.

Both address PA14 quorum sensing analysis (C90-C98). OpenEval details redundancy of rhlI and pqsE, peer reviewers affirm identification of quorum sensing regulators. Strong agreement on genetic mechanisms, with peer reviewers explicitly supporting these findings.

Addresses transmission assay validation of genetic effects (C99-C103). Both support that quorum sensing mutations affect transmission. Peer reviewers validate the overall genetic approach, consistent with OpenEval's SUPPORTED rating.

Both address supernatant experiments (C104-C105). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting limitations of negative results. Peer review also UNCERTAIN with Reviewer 3 directly challenging the claim, stating data only show GFP levels and don't confirm lack of effect on viral infection rate/load. Strong agreement on insufficient evidence.

Both address systematic genetic screen (C106-C110). OpenEval emphasizes screen design and specificity of hits, peer reviewers affirm methodological rigor. Both support the screen results and selective identification of virulence genes affecting viral transmission.

Perfect claim overlap (C113-C116) on P. lurida gacA analysis. Both support the finding that gacA deletion suppresses viral attenuation and the inference about conservation across Pseudomonas species. Complete agreement on this genetic mechanism.

Both address negative results for three genes in P. lurida (C117-C119). Both support these findings as valid negative results demonstrating species-specific differences. Peer reviewers accept the species-specific genetic patterns.

Perfect claim overlap (C120-C121, C124-C125) on bacterial mixing experiments. Both support the finding that P. lurida can override O. vermis pro-viral effects and the colonization mechanism. Complete agreement on bacterial competition results.

Both address electron microscopy observations (C129-C131). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN emphasizing speculation about glycocalyx promoting infection. Peer reviewers SUPPORT the descriptive findings while recognizing mechanistic hypothesis requires testing. Modest difference in emphasis on speculative nature.

Partial overlap on synthesis of major findings (C132, C138). Both strongly support the quantitative three-order-of-magnitude range and species-specificity conclusions. OpenEval synthesizes multiple claim groups, peer reviewers validate the overarching quantitative findings.

Addresses synthesis of major findings (C132-C133, C138). Both strongly support the overarching conclusions about bacterial modulation of viral transmission. Peer reviewers call work 'important' and 'convincing' with 'high rigor.'

Both address overarching conclusions (C9-C11, C138). Both strongly support that bacteria modulate viral transmission through multiple mechanisms. All peer reviewers affirm this as 'important work' demonstrating bacterial effects on viral susceptibility. Complete agreement on main conclusions.

OpenEval evaluates P. aeruginosa PA14 protective effects (C53-C56) with GFP and FISH data. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses these claims, though findings are consistent with overall supported conclusions about Pseudomonas attenuation effects.

OpenEval evaluates utility of experimental system (C139-C140) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review result directly addresses these meta-level claims about the system's utility, though peer reviewers' overall positive assessment implies agreement.
